item.title: Charli xcx Shares ‘Rock Music’ Song Teaser, Says She’s Not Making a Rock Album
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host begins speaking]
Host: "Hey music lovers, welcome to the latest update on what's trending on Billboard. If you've been following Charli XCX, you might have thought she was working on a rock album. But, it turns out, that's not the case. At least, not in the way you might think."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Last month, Charli was featured in British Vogue, and it was reported that she had rock music in the works. But, on Friday, she posted a studio footage teaser on Instagram, and it's definitely not what you'd expect from a traditional rock album. The song, also called 'Rock Music', features guitar, but it's more hyper-pop in production."
[Clip of Charli XCX's Instagram video plays briefly]
Host: "In the video, Charli is seen brainstorming and recording vocals. She even shows off some of her lyrics, which include the line 'I think the dance floor is dead, now we're making rock music.' It's clear she's playing with the idea of rock music, but not in a way that's traditional or expected."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Charli herself said in that British Vogue interview, 'What's interesting for me is to bend the possibilities of what my perspective on that could be.' And, it seems, she's doing just that. Her upcoming album, which includes 'Rock Music', is actually about her relationship with art and how it gives her purpose in life."
[Music transitions to a softer tone]
Host: "Charli's last album, 'Brat', peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and she's been working on new music since then. Including a soundtrack for Emerald Fennell's 'Wuthering Heights' adaptation, which debuted at No. 1 on the Soundtracks chart. We can't wait to hear more from Charli XCX and see where her music takes her next."
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: "That's all for now. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next update. Don't forget to follow us for the latest music news and trends."
